overview.description: This skill provides an interactive debugging workflow for OpenShift playbooks in TechZone environments using the OpenShift MCP server. It guides users through retrieving environment details, connecting to clusters via MCP, and executing debugging commands through the MCP server's tools.
overview.when_to_use: Use this skill when users need to debug OpenShift playbooks, troubleshoot cluster issues, or investigate deployment problems in TechZone OpenShift environments.

mcp_server_integration.description: The OpenShift MCP server provides direct cluster interaction capabilities without requiring local CLI tools or kubeconfig management. All operations are performed through MCP tools that handle authentication and cluster access.

step.title: Prompt for Request/Environment ID
step.description: Ask the user for their TechZone request ID or environment ID to retrieve the OpenShift cluster details.
step.action: Use ask_followup_question to request the ID if not already provided.
step.example: <ask_followup_question> <question>What is your TechZone request ID or environment ID for the OpenShift cluster you want to debug?</question> <follow_up> <suggest>I have a request ID (24-character hex string)</suggest> <suggest>I have an environment ID (24-character hex string)</suggest> <suggest>I'm not sure which ID I have</suggest> </follow_up> </ask_followup_question>

step.title: Retrieve Environment Details
step.description: Use the appropriate MCP server to retrieve the environment details based on the ID type provided.

actions.action: Try techzone-get-request first if ID format is ambiguous
If request lookup fails with 404, try techzone-get-environment
Extract environment details including status, cluster info, and kubeconfig

step.bearer_token_location: .bob/mcp.json -> mcpServers -> techzone-request-mcp -> headers -> Authorization Extract the token after "Bearer "

step.title: Display Environment Status
step.description: Present a clear summary of the environment status and key details to help the user understand the current state.

information_to_display.item: Number of worker nodes and their configuration

status_interpretation.status: Cluster is operational and ready for debugging
Cluster is still being provisioned, wait before debugging
Cluster provisioning failed, check logs for errors
Cluster has been deleted, cannot debug

step.title: Connect to Cluster via OpenShift MCP
step.description: Use the OpenShift MCP server to establish connection to the cluster. The MCP server handles authentication and cluster access automatically using the kubeconfig from the environment details.

mcp_connection.description: The OpenShift MCP server provides tools that interact directly with the cluster without requiring local CLI installation or manual kubeconfig setup.
mcp_connection.authentication: The MCP server extracts and uses the kubeconfig from the TechZone environment automatically. No manual kubeconfig setup is required.

advantages.advantage: Direct cluster interaction through MCP tools

configuration.description: Configure the OpenShift MCP server with the kubeconfig from the environment. This is done automatically by passing the kubeconfig content to the MCP server.

step.title: Verify Cluster Connection via MCP
step.description: Use OpenShift MCP tools to verify cluster connectivity and retrieve basic cluster information.

tool.name: get_cluster_version
tool.description: Retrieve OpenShift cluster version and update status
tool.use_case: Verify cluster is accessible and check version
tool.mcp_call: Use openshift-mcp server tools to get cluster version

tool.name: list_nodes
tool.description: List all nodes in the cluster with status
tool.mcp_call: Use openshift-mcp server tools to list nodes

tool.name: get_cluster_operators
tool.description: List OpenShift cluster operators and their health status
tool.mcp_call: Use openshift-mcp server tools to get operator status

step.title: Interactive Debugging Menu with MCP Tools
step.description: Present an interactive menu of debugging options using OpenShift MCP server tools. All operations are performed through MCP without requiring local CLI tools.

option.name: View Cluster Events
option.description: See recent cluster events to identify issues

parameters.parameter: limit: Number of events to retrieve

option.name: List Pods in Namespace
option.description: View all pods in a specific namespace

option.name: View Pod Logs
option.description: Retrieve logs from a specific pod

parameters.parameter: container: Optional container name for multi-container pods
previous: Get logs from previous container instance
tail: Number of lines to retrieve

option.name: Describe Resource
option.description: Get detailed information about a resource

parameters.parameter: resource_type: Type of resource (pod, deployment, service, etc.)
namespace: Namespace to search for jobs

option.name: Check ConfigMaps and Secrets
option.description: View configuration data used by playbooks
option.note: Secrets values are base64-encoded and should not be displayed

option.name: Check Node Status
option.description: View detailed node information and resource usage

parameters.parameter: resource_type: Type of resource to query

step.menu_presentation: Use ask_followup_question to present the menu and get user selection

step.title: Execute Debugging Commands via MCP
step.description: Execute the selected debugging commands using OpenShift MCP server tools and present the results to the user.

mcp_execution.description: All debugging operations are performed through the OpenShift MCP server. Use use_mcp_tool to call the appropriate OpenShift MCP server tools.

result_interpretation.guideline: Analyze command output for common issues
Highlight errors, warnings, or unusual patterns
Suggest next steps based on findings
Offer to execute related commands for deeper investigation

step.title: Offer Follow-Up Actions
step.description: Based on the debugging results, offer relevant follow-up actions to help the user resolve issues or gather more information.

suggested_actions.action: View pod logs to identify error
Check if image exists and is accessible

step.title: Session Summary
step.description: Provide a summary of the debugging session.
step.note: No cleanup is required when using the OpenShift MCP server, as it handles all authentication and connection management internally.

solutions.solution: Verify ID is correct (24 hex characters)
Check if request has been deleted
Check if environment has been deleted
Try retrieving by request ID instead
Check if environment is in Ready status
Check if platform supports kubeconfig download

error.name: mcp_server_not_available
error.symptom: OpenShift MCP server is not configured or not responding

solutions.solution: Verify openshift-mcp server is configured in .bob/mcp.json
Check MCP server is running and accessible
Fall back to traditional CLI-based debugging if needed

error.name: cluster_not_accessible
error.symptom: MCP server cannot connect to cluster

solutions.solution: Verify cluster is in Ready status

best_practices.practice: Always verify environment status before attempting to debug
Use OpenShift MCP server for seamless cluster interaction
Provide clear explanations of what each operation does
Interpret command output and highlight important information
Offer context-aware follow-up actions based on findings
Keep the debugging session interactive and guided
Handle errors gracefully with helpful suggestions
Leverage MCP tools to avoid local CLI tool dependencies

consideration.name: Never Display Sensitive Data
consideration.description: Do not display secret values, API keys, passwords, or other sensitive information from kubeconfig or cluster resources.

consideration.name: MCP Server Security
consideration.description: The OpenShift MCP server handles authentication securely. Ensure the MCP server configuration in .bob/mcp.json is properly secured.

consideration.name: Cluster Access Logging
consideration.description: All cluster access through the MCP server should be logged for audit purposes.

example_interaction.title: Complete Debugging Session with MCP
example_interaction.interaction:
User: "Debug my OpenShift playbook"
Bob: "I'll help you debug your OpenShift playbook using the OpenShift MCP server. What is your TechZone request ID or environment ID?"
User: "69dff2a2df7b5e69455106b0"
Bob: "Let me retrieve your environment details..."
[Executes techzone-get-environment]
Bob: "✓ Environment Retrieved
Status: Ready Name: OpenShift Cluster OCPv IBM Cloud OCP Version: 4.19 Cluster ID: itz-5sm6qr Worker Nodes: 3 nodes (4 vCPU x 16 GB each)
The cluster is operational. Connecting to cluster via OpenShift MCP server..."
[Connects via OpenShift MCP]
Bob: "✓ Successfully connected to cluster via MCP!
What would you like to debug? 1. View cluster events 2. List pods in namespace 3. View pod logs 4. Describe resource 5. Check playbook jobs 6. Check ConfigMaps and Secrets 7. Check cluster operators 8. Check node status 9. Execute custom query"
User: "Check playbook jobs"
Bob: "Which namespace should I check? (or 'all' for all namespaces)"
User: "default"
[Executes MCP tool: list_jobs with namespace=default]
Bob: "Found 2 jobs in default namespace: - post-deploy-mongodb: Failed (0/1 completions) - pre-cleanup-backup: Completed (1/1 completions)
The post-deploy-mongodb job failed. Would you like me to: 1. View the job logs 2. Describe the job for more details 3. Check the job pod status"
User: "View the job logs"
[Executes MCP tool: get_pod_logs for job pod]
Bob: "Here are the logs from the failed job:
[Log output showing error]
I can see the job failed due to a connection timeout to MongoDB. This suggests: - MongoDB service may not be ready - Network policy might be blocking connection - MongoDB pod might not be running
Would you like me to: 1. Check if MongoDB pods are running 2. View MongoDB pod logs 3. Check service endpoints 4. Return to debugging menu"

trigger_detection.description: The mode should automatically activate this skill when users mention debugging OpenShift, troubleshooting clusters, or investigating playbook issues.

mode_context.description: This skill complements the existing IBM TechZone Content Engineer mode by providing operational debugging capabilities for deployed environments using the OpenShift MCP server for seamless cluster interaction.
